title: Supreme Court orders Thiruparankundram lamp lit at hilltop pillar, issues contempt notices
dek: Finding a 'brazen violation' of its earlier order, the court suspended the temple's trustees, appointed two former judges to run it and summoned Tamil Nadu's Chief Secretary and DGP.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Supreme Court on Friday ordered that the ceremonial lamp be lit at the Deepathoon stone pillar on Thiruparankundram hill near Madurai on Saturday, 28 November, and issued contempt notices to 13 Tamil Nadu officials and temple trustees, including the Chief Secretary and the Director General of Police, after its earlier order for a one-time lighting on 24 November was not carried out.

A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi said there was prima facie a "brazen violation" of its 20 November order, suspended the temple's board of trustees and appointed two former Madras High Court judges as receivers to run the temple and carry out its directions, according to reports from the courtroom. It also vacated its earlier stay on the High Court's findings about the Deepathoon. The officials named must appear in person on 15 December.

## Friday's order

The court directed that the lamp be lit at the Deepathoon using the flame from the Uchi Pillaiyar mandapam if it is still burning, or by another arrangement, according to reports. In a change from its earlier order, which allowed only a team approved by the temple to light it, any devotee may now take part, provided they stay at least 50 metres from the Sikandar dargah on all sides. The Central Reserve Police Force is to guard both the temple and the dargah, and the safeguards for the dargah in the earlier order still apply.

The two receivers are the former High Court judges S. Vaidyanathan and V. Parthiban. The Chief Secretary must file an affidavit setting out the full sequence of events, including the communications and emails exchanged before 24 November.

The contempt notices went to the Chief Secretary, M. Sai Kumar; the DGP, Mahesh Agarwala; the HR&CE secretary and commissioner; the Madurai Collector, Nishanth Krishna; the Madurai Superintendent of Police; an HR&CE joint commissioner; the temple's executive officer, G. Selvi; and the chairman and four members of its board of trustees, according to reports.

The Collector had told the court that he could not carry out the order because the temple board had resolved that, by custom, the lamp could be lit only at the mandapam. The court rejected that. It called the Collector's status report "shedding crocodile tears" and the board's resolution an attempt to "overreach" its order through a "strained interpretation", and said the failure to light the lamp, read with the resolution, prima facie showed "wilful and flagrant disobedience", according to reports.

> "There is prima facie administrative chaos in the State of Tamil Nadu, at least in Madurai District," the bench said, according to reports.

It said executive authorities "seem to have acted on the dictates of their political bosses" and that the matter had to be unearthed, adding: "Time has come to deal with such situations with an iron hand, otherwise, it will lead to Constitutional chaos." No response from the Tamil Nadu government to Friday's order had been reported by the evening.

## What happened on 24 November

On the festival day, the Karthigai Deepam was lit at its customary spot on the hill, not at the hilltop pillar where the Supreme Court had allowed a one-time lighting this year, setting up the contempt fight between Hindu petitioners and Tamil Nadu's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government.

A small team of priests from the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy temple lit the Maha Deepam at the Uchi Pillaiyar Deepa Mandapam, as in past years, while police guarded the Deepathoon pillar near the summit, according to reports. Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran was stopped on his way to the hill, police removed protesters at the foothills after the ceremony, and the petitioners' lawyer said he would now ask the Supreme Court to begin contempt proceedings.

## The 20 November order

The Supreme Court's order of 20 November allowed the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon on 24 November, the day of the festival, as what the bench called a temporary, one-time arrangement. Under the order, the Madurai District Collector was the nodal officer and was to settle the composition of the lighting team with the temple's executive officer, the Archaeological Survey of India and the city police commissioner. No members of the public were to go with the team, and observances at customary locations were to continue undisturbed. The lighting was set for 6 pm, according to reports.

## Background

The dispute is over where the lamp should be lit. Thiruparankundram hill is home both to the Murugan temple at its base and to the Sikandar Badusha dargah at its summit; the Deepathoon is a stone pillar about 50 metres from the dargah. Successive state governments, under both the DMK and the AIADMK, have kept the lighting at the Uchi Pillaiyar mandapam, part-way up the hill.

In late 2025 a single judge of the High Court allowed the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon. The then DMK government refused, citing law and order, and the district administration imposed prohibitory orders; a High Court bench later found that its order had been wilfully disobeyed and ordered central security forces to provide protection. On 6 January 2026 a Division Bench upheld the single judge's ruling and rejected the state's argument that the pillar was a survey stone from British rule.

The TVK government, which took office this year under Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, kept the previous government's position. It filed an appeal in the Supreme Court on 11 June and said in June that it would hold the ritual at the usual location, putting social harmony first, according to reports. On 20 November the Supreme Court bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi stayed the High Court's findings while it hears the appeal, but allowed this year's one-time lighting, saying the arrangement neither accepted nor rejected either side's arguments. The state's Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) commissioner filed a petition the same day asking the court to review that interim order, according to reports.

## What they are saying

Mr Nagenthran has accused the TVK of copying what he calls the DMK's anti-Hindu stance on the issue. The Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), part of the TVK government, has strongly opposed lighting the lamp at the Deepathoon, and its leader Thol. Thirumavalavan had said the state would light it at the mandapam. The Left parties, which support the government from outside, share that position, according to reports. After 24 November the petitioners' lawyer, RM Arun Swaminathan, said there was "no other option except to file a contempt application", according to reports.

## What happens next

The lamp is due to be lit at the Deepathoon on Saturday under the receivers' supervision and CRPF security. The named officials and trustees must appear before the court on 15 December, when it will hear the contempt case. The state's review petition against the 20 November order and its main appeal against the High Court's January judgment, which will decide whether there is any customary right to light the lamp at the pillar in future years, are still pending.

## Timeline

- 6 Jan 2026: High Court Division Bench upholds order allowing lighting at the Deepathoon
- 11 Jun 2026: TVK government appeals to the Supreme Court
- 20 Nov 2026: Supreme Court stays High Court findings but allows a one-time lighting on 24 November; state seeks review
- 24 Nov 2026: Lamp lit at the Uchi Pillaiyar mandapam; petitioners say they will seek contempt
- 27 Nov 2026: Supreme Court orders lighting at the Deepathoon on 28 November, suspends temple trustees, issues contempt notices to 13 officials and trustees
